messages.author: cf19475e9feb9344
messages.subject: negative variance
parts:
Hi

I fit a mediation model and I get the following warning messages

Warning messages:
1: In lavaan::lavaan(model = model, data = fungal.r, ordered = c("inadequate_heating",  :
  lavaan WARNING: some estimated variances are negative
2: In lavaan::lavaan(model = model, data = fungal.r, ordered = c("inadequate_heating",  :
  lavaan WARNING: residual covariance matrix is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.ov") to investigate.

What does this mean?

Many thanks
Vasilis

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: negative variance
parts:
The two warnings are (almost certainly) about the same thing.  A residual variance is the part of the variance of a dependent variables that is not "explained" or accounted for by the predictors--equal to (1 – R2) times the total variance of the dependent variable.  Variances are supposed to be positive, and the same goes for variance components.  But your model gives rise to a residual variance that is negative.  This can happen due to random sampling error--where a very small true value will sometimes produce a negative estimate--but it can also be a sign of a problem in your model.
--Ed Rigdon
